note: Recast from the original description of Emerson 1952, in English; the alate and the soldier are both described. The soldier measurements are taken from table 5; the alate measurement table (table 4) survives in the OCR only as a header with the values missing, so no values are entered for it.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Both the alate and the soldier have 3 apical spurs on the fore tibia (2:2:2 in all the other species, except in individual specimens of araujoi), a primitive character retained in this species; the alate antenna has 15 segments and the soldier antenna 14, which is also the only combination in the genus. The sides of the soldier labrum are curved without lateral corners, and the margin behind the relatively wider, white median lobe is slightly concave.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown, the clypeus slightly paler than the head; fontanelle plate (when present) dark brown or pale yellow; pronotum margins as dark as the head but paler in the middle; tibiae slightly darker than the femora; wings hyaline, the costa and radius brown; abdominal tergites and sternites paler than the head and densely hairy. Y suture visible. Fontanelle plate sunken into a small point or a small oval plate, which may be smaller or larger than an ocellus. Compound eyes small, their lower margin 2/5 to 1/4 of an eye diameter from the lower margin of the head. Ocelli small, about one ocellus width or a little more from the compound eye. Postclypeus slightly longer than half its width. Antenna 15 segments. Posterior margin of the pronotum concave, the length large relative to the width. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, the upper one short. Closest to araujoi in the alate, differing mainly in body size; lespesii is smaller and has a shorter hind tibia.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Vertex with a few long setae and no short hairs, the underside without setae or hairs; postmentum with a few microscopic hairs and about 2 setae at the anterior end; anterior surface of the pronotum with short hairs. Sides of the head only slightly curved, almost flat and parallel. Frontal tube stout, thick at the base, reaching from above almost to the base of the anteclypeus and not upturned above the vertex. The narrowest part of the postmentum is about three fifths of the widest part (0.29:0.50 mm). Antenna 14 segments, segment 2 larger than segment 3, segment 3 larger than segment 4. Sides of the labrum curved without lateral corners, the margin behind the relatively wide, white median lobe slightly concave. Mandibles as in figure 2A. Anterior margin of the pronotum not concave or very shallowly concave. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs (the outer one short), the other tibiae with 2 each (3:2:2). Measurements: head including mandibles 2.94—3.00, head length to the tip of the frontal tube 2.10—2.23, head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 2.12—2.13, head width 1.44—1.53, head thickness 1.29—1.33, frontal tube length 0.36—0.42, labrum width 0.44, left mandible length 1.07—1.27, right mandible length from the notch 0.54, pronotum length 0.53—0.54, width 0.85—0.87, hind tibia length 1.06—1.22 mm (n=1—3). Type locality Brazil; the type specimens are 2 alates identified by Hagen, and specimens from La Sierra, Uruguay and Salta, Argentina were also identified by Silvestri and Holmgren.
